description: I am interested in engineering, data science and coding. Also enjoy doing interesting challenges.
summary: Ridgeback is a browser tool for planning Mars exploration in Jezero crater while using real NASA and USGS data. It combines elevation, images, slope, geology, night time infrared and sand maps from three NASA missions into a 2D map and a 3D landscape you can drive. The users will drive a solar rover built to real NASA limits with safe routes, and astronauts can plan Marswalks that show the safest path there and back and also how long it takes. This gives explorers one view for deciding where to go and whether or not they can return safely, which matters because on Mars there is no one to help or rescue.
details: Our app is a browser-based planning tool for a real 30 x 23 km area of Jezero crater. We used NASA and USGS data such as, images and elevation from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, night-time infrared from Mars Odyssey, slope worked out from the elevation, and the USGS geologic map. This was all shown on a 2D map and a 3D landscape. The users on the app will drive Ridgeback, which is a solar rover based on Curiosity and Perseverance. The app chooses the fastest, safest, or more balanced routes that avoid steep slopes and deep sand while also managing the battery at the same time. Astronauts can plan Marswalks because the app finds the safest round trip, shows the time it takes and also warns about risky grounds, while using NASA's spacewalk limits. The benefit of the app is seeing hazards, warnings, and whether you can get back, before you commit. We hope it shows how open NASA data can make missions safer and gets the public exploring real Mars terrain and environment. We built this project with JavaScript, HTML, CSS and three.js, and prepared the data with Python, hosted it on Vercel and used Claude Code as an AI assistant. It doesn't need any special hardware. It is creative because it turns scientific maps into something you can drive and also links the rover and astronaut into one mission. We focused on accuracy, safety, and realistic limits.
